concept.reason: Real skull with10cm scale and restored cast sufficient.

scope: Original whole organism, two tall curved horns rising from rear frill. Not skull-only.
specimen_basis: UMNH VP16699, Last Chance skull. Original left skull and restored cast distinguished.

scale.primary_anchor: Original2007 discoverers report beak-to-frill about1m, paired spines add0.5m, brow horns0.25m. Confirm photograph10cm scale.
scale.body_length_status: Explicit modelling estimate, not measured whole specimen. Body inferred from related quadrupedal ceratopsids.
scale.conflict: Modern UGS summary says4.5ft beak-to-frill versus2007 original1m; use original authors metric and true scale image, not false precision.

diagnostic_targets: Tall tapering frill, narrows toward upper rear, two tall terminal horns curve upward and outward/sideways; clearly separate negative space.
Two prominent upright brow horns, shorter than rear frill horns. NOT Einiosaurus rounded brows.
Short deep snout, low nasal ornament, no long curved Einiosaurus nasal horn.
Blade-like projecting cheek processes; small subordinate frill edge nodes.
Full heavy quadruped body, short neck, four connected weight-bearing limbs, tapering tail.
uncertainties: Skull-based fossil, body shape/tail/skin/colour inferred, not a complete fossil skeleton.
Restore bilateral missing anatomy; bone openings covered by living tissues, no open windows through living frill.
Museum dates79.5Ma versus UGS82Ma differ; retain Late Cretaceous Campanian without overprecise time.
acceptance_checks: Front/top show paired rear horns with outward curves.
Side silhouette deep snout, tall rear frill, long brow horns and low nose ornament.
Do not copy Einiosaurus straight rear spikes or curled nasal horn.
handoff_contract: Same dir prep maker QA. Maker fixedhash COMPLETE stops; root asynchronous backup; local-first integration; no maker upload cleanup.
